newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1997 budget draft seen ready by October 10.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1997 budget draft seen ready by October 10.

text.p: Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko on Wednesday said he would finish work on his draft of Poland's 1997 budget by October 10 but he expected government and parliamentary debates on it to be difficult.
"The budget draft will be submitted to the government on October 10," Kolodko said at a meeting with foreign reporters.
He confirmed that the draft would be designed to bring year-on-year inflation to about 13 percent in December 1997 from 21.6 percent in December last year and about 17 percent expected for this year.
He also confirmed he would propose to set the 1997 budget deficit at an equivalent of 2.6 percent of gross domestic product, whose growth is expected to be maintained at 5.5 percent next year.

But he said he expected it would be difficult to push his ambitious plans through the cabinet of the ruling left-wing coalition of ex-communists and a peasant party, especially since parliamentary elections are due next year.
"The issue has died down at the moment...but after October 10 we may see a small war," he said.
"Sometimes I feel isolated in my fight against inflation," he added, suggesting that his cabinet colleagues and parliamentarians might want to boost budgetary spending.
The government will have until the end of October to approve the budget draft and send it to parliament. Parliament will then have three months to suggest amendments and pass it, or face dissolution.
